title: The Pawn That Was Never Free
setup: Black answered the Spanish bishop with the knight to d4, and White's knight has just grabbed a pawn. Attack that knight and a loose pawn with one move.
hint: The greedy knight and the g-pawn are both unguarded. Find the one square that looks at each of them.
explanation:
## The Idea

The Spanish bishop never really attacked e5, and White has just grabbed the pawn anyway.

{{Qg5}} hits the knight on e5 and the g2 pawn at once. White should cut the losses now; keep grabbing with {{Nxf7}}, and {{Qxg2}}, {{Rf1}} {{Qxe4+}}, {{Be2}} ends in {{Nf3#}}, mate by the knight that started on d4.

Taking the bishop with {{Nxb5}} is just as strong. The queen move shows why the pawn was never free.
